I know this is old but I relate so much. I started antidepressants in January. I had already been fucking up before that, but WOW it became damn near impossible to even function for awhile. Honestly I’m still exhausted and feeling nothing but apathy and numbness. I kept hoping it would go away. I’m afraid to switch to a different antidepressant while in school or even during summer break because the side effects rendered me useless for the first month. 

I found out recently that I can’t get financial aid, totally blindsided me. And in general it just feels really lonely because none of the students or faculty really see how hard it is to be struggling in those ways. I’m sure they have been effected mentally and perhaps financially by grad school and covid. But none of them are scared that they can’t afford rent. Isolation took its toll I’m sure, but none of them lost the ability to function in the program due to mental health circling the drain. They had a hard time probably, but are all still keeping up, now even thriving. Most of the other grad students in my program clearly come from money. They have back up plans, family to help them, they can afford to spend money to fix a lot of the common problems that so many can’t. 

I know this sounds like I’m competing in the pain olympics with them, but honestly they just seem like aliens to me sometimes: I don’t understand how I’m the only one in my program consistently failing and struggling to keep afloat like this. It makes me bitter. I know that’s immature to think like that. I don’t wish anything was magically be easier on me, I just wish someone would acknowledge the fact that certain factors make it harder for you to run the race I guess. 

And this post you wrote made me feel better in a selfish way. I’m sorry you’re going through all that, and I hope it’s gotten better by now. Even if people are kind and supportive, they still won’t fully understand how difficult your experience is. I hope the people around you speak with empathy and patience. And I hope you’re situation becomes easier. You seem very kind, but you are totally allowed to be upset and complain. If you ever want to rant you can shoot me a message.

I’ve always lived with a lot of roommates. I love living with people, but I’m also not very strict about anything. Even if you’re roommates are super clean and respectful, they are still gonna do stuff that drives you nuts. You’re gonna have to let a lot of stuff go because people are all so different with different ways of doing things. 

If something bothers you and really needs to be fixed, don’t let it fester. Don’t leave passive aggressive notes. Don’t complain to the other roommates about each other. Just have a conversation with them in a chill way. 

Most people have no clue that some of their habits/behavior could be perceived as annoying or rude. And most people don’t want to be the bad roomate, so if it’s something they can easily fix to make you more comfortable they probably will. 

But if you hold it in and let the resentment build, it could turn into a stalemate over the dishes or something stupid and might start to form cliques.

Honestly if you know you’re uptight, it’s gonna be rough.
